_readme: Fill this file in and the page is done — nothing in index.html or scripts/ should need editing. Anything set to null disappears from the page. Run `node scripts/validate-config.js` when you are finished. See SETUP.md.

page.title: TODO Parliamentary election in <Jurisdiction> · <Year>
page._postUrlComment: The WordPress post this page is embedded in. Used by scripts/check-embed.js, which is the only thing that looks at it — the page never calls back to the post. Set it once the post exists.
page._pagesUrlComment: Where this page is published, e.g. https://europe-elects.github.io/<repo>/. Publish it alongside the article: it is served from a CDN and executes no PHP, so it stays up when the WordPress host does not.

election.title: TODO Parliamentary election in <Jurisdiction>

jurisdiction._comment: `territory` is the sub-national unit for a regional election — a German Land, a Spanish comunidad autónoma, an Italian regione, a Belgian region, a devolved UK nation. Leave it null for a national election. `territoryNative` is the local-language spelling, used only where the page shows it alongside the English one; null repeats `territory`.

election._firstProjectionComment: When the first projection is expected, if the pollsters publish one. null removes that sentence from the page.
election._seatsTotalComment: Size of the chamber being elected. Used to sanity-check seat figures coming out of the Sheet. null for a presidential election, or where seats are not reported.
election._ballotNameComment: What the counted vote is called locally, e.g. "list vote", "second vote (Landesstimme)", "regional list vote". null omits it.

previous._comment: The election this one is compared against. Set the whole object to null where there is no comparable predecessor — a newly created assembly, or a first election under a new franchise.

sheet.id: TODO paste the Sheet ID out of its URL
sheet._tabsComment: Tabs are referenced by NAME, never by gid. A gid is regenerated every time a Sheet is duplicated; the name survives. Names are case-sensitive and must match the tab exactly, spaces and punctuation included. Set a tab to null when that tab does not exist for this election — the section that depends on it is then dropped.

results._comment: Layout of the `results` tab. Column 0 is always the party name; these are the 0-based indexes of the rest. Set `seats`, `changeVotes` or `changeSeats` to null where the tab does not carry that column — a presidential first round has no seats, and a first-ever election has nothing to change against.
results._totalRowComment: Case-insensitive regular expression matching the label of the totals row, so it is summed as an electorate figure rather than mistaken for a party.

sheet._ignoredTabsComment: Tabs the Apps Script should NOT treat as a reason to rebuild — working tabs that feed nothing on the page. Deliberately a deny-list: forgetting to list a tab costs one wasted no-op run, whereas an allow-list fails silently and loses data.

source._localPathComment: Path to a local PartiesData checkout, e.g. "../PartiesData". When set it is read instead of GitHub, which is how this runs offline and without a token. Leave null in the committed config — the Action has no checkout to read.
source._authComment: PartiesData is a private repository, so the build reads it through the GitHub Contents API with a token from PARTIESDATA_TOKEN (a fine-grained PAT with Contents: Read on it). In the Action that is a repository secret of the same name. See SETUP.md.
source._comment: `continent` picks the file (<continent>/partiesdata.yaml). `country` and `electionType` are the first two YAML keys inside it and must match verbatim. PartiesData files sub-national elections two different ways, and both work here: as an election type under the country — country "Germany" with electionType "Saxony-Anhalt regional parliament" (also "Berlin regional parliament", "Mecklenburg-Vorpommern regional") — or as a top-level key of its own, where country is "Belgium (Flanders)", "United Kingdom (Scotland)", "Greenland (Denmark)" and electionType is "national parliament". Run `node scripts/fetch-parties.js --list` to print what actually exists for a country before guessing.

parties._requireSourceComment: Set false when the territory has no PartiesData entry at all — plenty of regions do not. The build then does not fail on a missing entry, and every party has to come from `metadataFallback` and `extra` instead.
parties._metadataFallbackComment: Entries tried, in order, for a party the primary entry does not list — for a regional election that would typically be [{ "country": "Germany", "electionType": "national parliament" }]. Only ep_group, colour and full name are taken from a fallback; `last_results` never is, because a national result is not a regional baseline.
parties._baselineSourceComment: Where the previous-election figure in the results table comes from. "partiesdata" reads `last_results` off the entry named in `source` — correct when that entry really is this territory's own last election. "content" reads content/previous-result.json instead, which is what you want when the only PartiesData entry available is the national one. "none" drops the column.
parties._orderComment: Display order as a list of template codes. Empty keeps PartiesData's own order.

overrides._comment: Keyed by the party's key in PartiesData. Every field is optional — anything omitted is derived: `code` from the key (uppercased, de-accented), `name` as "<key> (<ep_group>)", `color` from the party's own PartiesData `color:` and otherwise from europarty-palette.json, `euro` as "<europarty> (<ep_group>)". `aliases` adds spellings the Sheet may use; the key, the code and the display name already match automatically. Delete the example below.

EXAMPLE — delete me.name: Animal Welfare Party
aliases: alternative spelling used in the Sheet

extra._comment: Parties PartiesData does not carry and will not — historic ones that appear only in a long polling series, or regional parties below the national radar. Same fields as an override, but `name` and `color` are required because there is nothing to derive them from. With `requireSource: false` this is where the whole party list lives. Delete the example below.

sections._comment: The page is built from these, in this order. Set any section to null to remove it completely — heading, card and fetches all go. `label` is the coloured band, `heading`/`sub`/`note` the card text. Charts are Datawrapper embeds: `id` is the 5-character chart ID, `version` the published version in the embed URL (a fresh copy starts at 1), `live: true` means the chart reads the Sheet and the Action republishes it on every update.

records._comment: Ranked comparison lists — a party's best results, its biggest gains, the weakest showing for a governing party. Each block is defined in content/records.json; this section only switches them on.

automation._githubRepoComment: Used by scripts/ for log lines and by SETUP.md. The Action itself uses $GITHUB_REPOSITORY and the Apps Script reads its own GITHUB_REPO script property, so a wrong value here breaks nothing.
automation._sheetFallbackComment: The page reads the generated JSON first and only falls back to reading the Sheet directly every Nth cycle — the Sheet sends no-store, so every reader hitting it goes to Google unbuffered.
